correctness.rationale: For the lower bound, the full-action invariant-measure simplex is contained in the subgroup-invariant simplex. For the upper bound, left-coset averaging converts every subgroup-invariant measure into a full-action invariant measure; a joint refinement of the coset-translated starting cover and repeated use of Meyerovitch Lemma 2.4 produce a refinement whose pointwise order is at most the sum of the translated orders. Integration turns that sum exactly into the subgroup index times an integral against the averaged full-action invariant measure. Empty invariant-measure simplices occur simultaneously, the infinite-dimension case is immediate, and the finite-orbit cyclic-layer example verifies sharpness using the published orbit-size formula.

value.rationale: Finite-index restriction is a basic structural operation for group actions, and Meyerovitch explicitly uses finite-index subgroups to express periodic-point obstructions. The theorem quantifies exactly how much the new invariant can change under that operation and shows the coefficient is optimal. For \(\mathbb Z\)-systems it gives a sharp power law under passage from \(F\) to \(F^q\), which is directly relevant when sampling an orbit at a coarser cadence. The proof is short but not a renaming: it couples a genuinely enlarged invariant-measure simplex with coset averaging and cover-order subadditivity, and the factor can be attained.
